methodological_rigor.justification: The study has a reasonable comparative design with 58 LUAD patients balanced across KRASmt/wt and early/late stage (15/14 each cell), and uses an appropriate highly sensitive ddPCR technique with an empirically derived ≥3-events threshold referencing a Bio-Rad protocol. However, no power calculation is reported, EV characterization (western blot, TRPS, TEM) was performed on only a single representative sample rather than systematically, and comprehensive quantification of EV vs cfDNA proportions was not done per case (acknowledged as a limitation). Pre-analytical heterogeneity is a notable issue: P1/P2 were isolated before storage while P3 was isolated after thawing, and pellets were resuspended in remnant plasma causing cfDNA/albumin co-contamination — acknowledged but limits interpretation of EV-specific findings. Statistically, Fisher's exact test, Cohen's kappa, and one-way ANOVA are appropriate for the data types, but there is no correction for multiplicity across the 4 fractions × 2 stage strata comparisons, no sensitivity analyses, and no confidence intervals reported for sensitivity/specificity estimates in Table 3.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy comparison of an index test (ddPCR on four plasma fractions) against a reference standard (tumor NGS) in 58 LUAD patients enriched by known mutation status — effectively a case-control-style diagnostic study with pre-selected KRASmt and KRASwt arms, mapping to Oxford LoE 3b. Clinical relevance is moderate: KRAS G12C is now targetable (adagrasib/sotorasib) and plasma genotyping is clinically important, but the main message — that unfractionated plasma SUP (cfDNA) outperforms EV-enriched fractions and achieves 92.9% sensitivity in late-stage disease — essentially corroborates existing cfDNA-based liquid biopsy practice rather than offering a new assay. The negative finding for EV fractions in early-stage LUAD limits translational enthusiasm, and the ultracentrifugation workflow is explicitly acknowledged as not clinically deployable.

reporting_quality.justification: The most applicable checklist is STARD given the diagnostic accuracy framing (index test = ddPCR per fraction; reference = tumor NGS). Methods are reasonably detailed for assays, reagents, centrifugation parameters, thresholding, and ethics approvals, and Table 3 reports sensitivity, specificity, PPA, NPA, OPA, and kappa. Key STARD gaps include: no flow diagram of participant selection/exclusions, no reporting of indeterminate results handling beyond the L14/P3 technical exclusion, no 95% CIs around diagnostic accuracy estimates, no explicit pre-specification of threshold prior to analysis (the ≥3 threshold is derived in a Supporting Information section), and limited reporting on timing between tumor NGS and plasma collection. Data availability is weak: no deposition of ddPCR raw droplet data, no analysis code, and supplementary tables referenced but no repository identifier mentioned in the blinded text.

novelty_literature.justification: The empirical novelty is incremental: the study extends prior ddPCR/EV comparisons (previously done in colon [ref 17] and pancreatic [ref 18] cancer) to LUAD, and partially replicates the recent finding by Moldovan et al. [ref 20] that small-EV DNA is not enriched for tumor DNA in lung cancer. The main finding — that unfractionated plasma SUP outperforms EV-enriched fractions for KRAS detection in LUAD — is directionally opposite to the pancreatic/colon cancer EV-advantage literature, which adds some tumor-type-specific nuance, but does not introduce a new assay, mechanism, or framework. The MFA observation (higher mutant-to-wildtype ratio in EV fractions despite lower absolute copies) has been reported previously in BRAF/colorectal contexts [ref 35], so it is confirmatory rather than novel.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written with a logical structure: the introduction frames the EV-vs-cfDNA question well, methods are described in sufficient operational detail, and the discussion thoughtfully contextualizes the discordant findings relative to pancreatic/colon cancer literature. The abstract is self-contained and quantitatively grounded (specific detection counts per fraction and stage). Figure captions are informative and standalone-interpretable; Table 3 is appropriately labeled. Minor issues include some redundancy between results and discussion regarding the SUP-vs-EV comparison, inconsistent reporting of TRPS pressure values in Results (200/400/600 Pa) vs Methods (200/400/800 Pa), and lengthy discussion of the single false-positive case L21 that could be tightened.

key_strengths: Balanced 2×2 design (KRASmt/wt × early/late stage) with 58 well-characterized LUAD cases and tumor NGS as reference standard
Technically sound ddPCR workflow with explicit, empirically derived ≥3-event threshold and false-positive assay
Multi-modal EV characterization (western blot, TRPS, TEM) consistent with MISEV2023 nomenclature guidance
Clear, honest discussion of pre-analytical limitations (P1/P2 vs P3 storage asymmetry, cfDNA/albumin co-contamination, small 2.5 mL plasma volume)
Clinically useful negative finding that EV-enriched fractions do not outperform unfractionated SUP in LUAD, contrasting prior pancreatic/colon reports
key_concerns: No power calculation, no multiplicity correction across 4 fractions × 2 stages, and no 95% CIs around sensitivity/specificity estimates in Table 3
EV characterization performed on only one representative case rather than systematically — undermines quantitative claims about EV content per fraction
Pre-analytical asymmetry between P1/P2 (isolated pre-storage) and P3 (post-thaw) confounds between-fraction comparisons
STARD reporting gaps: no flow diagram, no pre-specification of index-test threshold, limited handling of indeterminate results, no data/code deposition
Novelty is incremental and partially confirmatory of recent lung-cancer work (ref 20); ultracentrifugation workflow has no near-term clinical translational path by the authors' own admission
Early-stage detection sensitivity near 0% across all fractions limits the practical message to 'cfDNA works in late-stage LUAD' — already established
chief_reviewer.rationale: A technically competent but incremental descriptive comparison that essentially corroborates established cfDNA plasma genotyping in late-stage LUAD and reports a negative result for EV-enriched fractions; with modest sample size, no power/multiplicity treatment, limited EV characterization depth, and no clear translational path, the paper fits a Tier 4 journal (e.g., focused specialty or methods journal) after minor revisions to tighten STARD reporting and add confidence intervals.
